documents.text: In an ideal DC resistive circuit, voltage V in volts equals current I in amperes times resistance R in ohms: V = IR. For positive resistance, doubling V at fixed R doubles I. In series, the same current flows through all resistors and equivalent resistance is their sum. Two series resistors of 2 ohms and 4 ohms have equivalent resistance 6 ohms; on a 12 V source current is 2 A. Voltage drops are 4 V and 8 V, summing to the source voltage.

In parallel each branch has the same voltage. The reciprocal equivalent resistance is the sum of reciprocal branch resistances. Two 6-ohm parallel resistors have equivalent resistance 3 ohms. On a 12 V supply each branch carries 2 A, so total current is 4 A. Power P = VI = I^2 R = V^2/R for an ideal resistor; units are watts. At fixed voltage a smaller resistance dissipates more power, but at fixed current a larger resistance dissipates more power. State which quantity is fixed before comparing power. An ideal ammeter is inserted in series and an ideal voltmeter in parallel.

cases.excluded: Incorrect answer key: two 6-ohm parallel resistors have resistance 12 ohms. Power is measured in amperes.

documents.text: A quadrat is a fixed-area sample used to estimate density of sessile organisms. Random placement reduces selection bias. In a synthetic meadow, five 2 m^2 quadrats contain 3, 5, 4, 6 and 2 daisies. Total sampled area is 10 m^2, total count 20, estimated density 2 daisies per m^2. Extrapolating to a comparable 150 m^2 meadow gives 300 daisies; this assumes samples represent the meadow. A larger sample reduces sampling variation but does not automatically remove systematic selection bias.

The simple mark-recapture estimate is N = M*C/R, where M animals were initially marked, C animals were caught later, and R of that later catch were marked. With M=40, C=50, R=10, N=200 animals. Assumptions: closed population between catches, marks retained and recognised, marked animals mix back into population, and equal capture probability. Migration or unequal catchability can bias estimates. If no marked animals are recaptured, division by zero prevents this simple estimate; it is not evidence of an infinite population. Quadrat sampling suits sessile plants; mark-recapture suits mobile animals. Correlation between rainfall and abundance alone does not establish causation because confounders may affect both.

cases.excluded: Incorrect field guide: no recaptures proves an infinite population; quadrat density uses the full meadow area as denominator.
